title: Ines and the Autopsy
premise: Ines Varga, a reclusive mortuary assistant, has spent years feeding anonymous tips to true-crime podcaster Theo Fairweather while hiding behind a fabricated identity. When a drowned woman surfaces wearing clothes lifted from Ines's closet, the police name Ines a person of interest, and Theo arrives in town to cover the story in person, unknowingly hunting his own ghost-writer. Together they decode a mortuary ledger whose embalming dates and initials map a decades-long string of 'accidents' tied to the town's founding families. At the anniversary dinner of the Ashcombe Historical Society, Ines exposes the killer—the beloved town archivist who murdered her own mother, the case that made Ines a witness as a child—choosing truth and her fragile found family with Theo over the invisibility she once believed kept her safe.
about_author: Marguerite Amberdale is the pen name of a former hospital archivist who spent fifteen years cataloguing unclaimed belongings and the stories they refused to tell. She writes mysteries from a converted chapel on the coast, where the fog does half her plotting.

chapters.title: The Weight of Quiet Things
chapters.summary: Ines Varga's POV. Ines prepares a body at Halloway & Sons mortuary, establishing her ritualized invisibility and her secret habit of mailing anonymous case tips to podcaster Theo Fairweather. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for safety, cracked by a flicker of longing to be known.

chapters.title: Clothes That Aren't Hers
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Police arrive: a drowned woman pulled from the reservoir wears Ines's own cardigan and scarf, items stolen from her closet. Detective Okafor questions her; Ines lies badly about the break-in she never reported. Emotional beat: the horror of being seen, framed in fabric.

chapters.title: Episode Forty-One
chapters.summary: Theo Fairweather's POV. Theo, mid-series on Ashcombe's 'accident' cluster, learns of the new death and realizes his anonymous source lives in the very town he's about to descend on. Emotional beat: obsessive thrill curdling into guilt that his show may have summoned a killer's attention.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Funeral Home
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Theo walks into the mortuary under a journalist's pretext; Ines recognizes his voice instantly and must play a stranger to the man she's corresponded with for years. Emotional beat: vertigo of intimacy and disguise colliding in one room.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines notices the mortuary's old embalming ledger contains initials and dates that don't match its official records—a coded second column. She photographs pages but hesitates to send them. Emotional beat: the pull of truth against the discipline of hiding.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo investigates the drowned woman, Dana Pell, and finds her death mirrors a 1987 'accident' from his podcast's coldest case. He begins mapping overlaps. Emotional beat: the hunter's cold clarity warming into genuine care for the victims.

chapters.title: Anniversary of Glass
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The Ashcombe Historical Society's anniversary dinner approaches; Ines is pressured by her employer to attend and cater the memorial toast. She glimpses the archivist, Vivian Marsh, handling old records with unsettling familiarity. Emotional beat: dread dressed as civic duty.

chapters.title: Two Names, One Handwriting
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Comparing the ledger's coded initials with historical society minutes, Theo finds the same handwriting signing both—Vivian's predecessor, and Vivian herself. He mails his findings to his anonymous source, not knowing she stands beside him at the copy shop. Emotional beat: dramatic irony as aching comedy.

chapters.title: The Break-In That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines discovers her apartment was entered not to steal but to plant: a duplicate ledger page tucked in her mattress, framing her as the code's author. She realizes the killer knows who she is. Emotional beat: terror of a sanctuary violated, invisibility revealed as a trap.

chapters.title: Confession by Voicemail
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, with Theo intercut. Ines finally leaves Theo a voicemail almost confessing everything, then deletes it. Theo, listening to his tip line, catches a fragment before it's erased. Emotional beat: the almost, and the cost of almost.

chapters.title: Dana's Last Week
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Reconstructing Dana Pell's final days: she was a genealogist hired by someone to trace the 1987 case—hired, Theo suspects, by Vivian to find out how much Dana knew. Emotional beat: grief for a stranger becoming personal.

chapters.title: The Second Autopsy
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines secretly re-examines Dana's body and finds marks inconsistent with drowning—restrained wrists, a pre-mortem head wound. She photographs evidence, now truly on the run's edge. Emotional beat: the mortician's oath to the dead over the living's comfort.

chapters.title: Okafor's Doubt
chapters.summary: Detective Okafor's POV. Okafor, pressured to close the case on Ines, privately retests the timeline and finds the planted evidence too neat. He begins an off-book inquiry. Emotional beat: institutional loyalty fracturing against conscience.

chapters.title: The Found Family Dinner
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo and Ines, identities nearly exposed to each other, share an uneasy meal at a diner and trade half-truths that land like full confessions. They agree—without saying it—to work together. Emotional beat: two loners recognizing each other's armor.

chapters.title: Decoding the Column
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Using embalming dates, Ines cracks the ledger's cipher: initials of twelve dead, all ruled accidents, all tied to the Historical Society's founding families—including her own mother, the 1987 case's forgotten victim. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into purpose.

chapters.title: Vivian's Kindness
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Vivian Marsh invites Ines for tea, warm and maternal, revealing she's known Ines's face since the 1987 funeral—she recognized the frightened child who saw something. Ines escapes politely. Emotional beat: the horror of kindness as surveillance.

chapters.title: The Tip Line Trap
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo traces a call to his tip line to the Historical Society's basement phone; someone has been listening to his source's messages for years. He realizes his podcast was Vivian's early-warning system. Emotional beat: the hunter learning he was bait.

chapters.title: What the Child Saw
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines finally recovers the suppressed memory: as a girl, she saw Vivian push her mother from the boathouse—and Vivian saw her seeing. Every 'accident' since was housekeeping; Ines's anonymity was Vivian's mercy or her waiting. Emotional beat: childhood terror reclaimed as adult testimony.

chapters.title: Okafor's Choice
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. Okafor confronts the planted evidence chain, finds the duplicate ledger page's paper matches Historical Society stock, and must decide whether to arrest his prime suspect or follow the trail to a pillar of the town. Emotional beat: a good officer choosing truth over career.

chapters.title: The Anniversary Dinner
chapters.summary: Ines and Theo, alternating. At the Historical Society's anniversary dinner, Vivian raises the memorial toast; Ines stands and reads the twelve names from the ledger aloud as Theo records. Vivian's mask slips; the room turns. Emotional beat: the climactic unmasking—truth spoken in the killer's own theater.

chapters.title: Boathouse Reckoning
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Vivian flees to the boathouse where it began, taking Ines at knife-point to finish the witness problem; Okafor and Theo intervene, and Vivian, cornered by her own recorded confession playing from Theo's phone, surrenders. Ines chooses not to run. Emotional beat: the past's stage revisited and rewritten.

chapters.title: Ines, By Name
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, epilogue weeks later. Ines testifies, signs her real name to her statements, and co-credits 'the source' on Theo's finale episode—then agrees to co-host a new series about the unnamed dead. The found family assembles at the diner. Emotional beat: invisibility traded, willingly and forever, for being known.
